what_its_for: Acamprosate helps people who have stopped drinking alcohol stay sober. It works by balancing certain chemicals in your brain that get out of balance when you stop drinking. It does NOT help with alcohol withdrawal symptoms, and it works best when used along with counseling or a support program.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Take your tablets with or without food, but taking them with meals may help you remember your doses. Try to take it at the same times every day.
dosing: The usual adult dose is TWO 333 mg tablets (totaling 666 mg) taken THREE times a day — once in the morning, once at midday, and once in the evening. Your doctor may adjust this dose if you have kidney problems.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store acamprosate at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep it out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication — the goal is to remain alcohol-free. Alcohol does not cause a dangerous reaction with acamprosate like some other medicines, but drinking will prevent the medication from working. Talk to your doctor before using other medicines that make you sleepy, such as sleep aids or anxiety medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, severe depression or sudden changes in mood or behavior, severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, trouble breathing), or severe diarrhea, vomiting, or stomach pain. Also contact your doctor if you feel unusually anxious, hopeless, or if you relapse and start drinking again.
when_it_works: Acamprosate may take a few days to build up in your system, but many people start to notice reduced cravings and urges to drink within the first week or two. For best results, keep taking it even if you feel well. Treatment is usually continued for about one year.
special_populations: Kidney problems: Your doctor will need to lower your dose or may tell you not to use this medicine if your kidneys do not work well. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medication. Older adults: Seniors may be more sensitive to side effects, especially dizziness. Children: Acamprosate is not approved for use in people under 18 years old.
